To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fructose administration to rats causes a 50% fall in renal tissue ATP concentration which does not adversely affect renal function.
the administration of a fructose infusion in the setting of a 30 min clamp ischemic insult does not result in any worsening of the functional or histologic consequences of ischemia.
fructose administration causes depletion of ATP in the renal medulla and does not affect renal functions or the recovery from ischemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of adenosine as a mediator of the renal response to ischemia.
the role of the renal vasculature in the pathogenesis of acute renal failure (ARF).
understanding the pathophysiology of ischemic acute renal failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the renal tissue concentrations of ATP are not critical to maintaining renal function in vivo, at least in the range of 50% depletion.
the tissue concentration of renal ATP is not an important determinant of the functional or histologic integrity of the kidney.
ATP depletion is a normal consequence of renal ischemia and that it is a marker of ischemic injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kidney is remarkably resilient to injury from ischemic insults and from the loss of ATP in the renal cortex.
ATP depletion does not affect the kidney function in the setting of normal conditions or ischemic conditions.
ATP depletion does not affect renal function in normal animals and that it does not affect recovery from ischemic insults.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tissue concentration of adenosine 5’-triphosphate (ATP), the main cellular energy source, does not have an important role in the regulation of renal function in the normal kidney or in the recovery from an ischemic insult.
the tissue concentration of adenosine is not a critical determinant of the functional and histologic integrity of the kidney.
the tissue concentration of adenine nucleotides is not a major determinant of renal function or injury in vivo.
